question: Does UnbackedClaims' evidence WINDOW carry any signal, or is proximity between a claim and evidence just an artifact of evidence density?

corpus.what: real assistant messages from local agent transcripts
corpus.bias_warning: This corpus is unusually evidence-dense because the system that produced it requires evidence in replies. That density is precisely why proximity carries little information here. On a sparser corpus proximity may carry real signal; re-run the null model before assuming this transfers.

labelling.backed: evidence exists ANYWHERE in the message, at any distance
labelling.unbacked: no evidence anywhere in the message
labelling.why: Neither label can be influenced by the window under test. Labelling by the gate's own current verdict would make the derived window reproduce the present window.

null_model: Same messages, same number of evidence lines, positions randomised. Only placement changes.
verdict: PROXIMITY CARRIES ALMOST NO SIGNAL. The shipped window of 2 performs about 4 points above random placement; every wider window performs at or BELOW it. A threshold derived from the coverage curve alone would have encoded evidence density while carrying the authority of a measurement.
what_survives: The BINARY signal. Every message with a claim and no evidence anywhere is caught at any window, so the check's value is intact and the window is a cheap heuristic sitting on top of a signal that works.
action_taken: The window was NOT re-derived. Its docstring now states what it is.
